**Finding submitted: deviation (MINCOMMIT), fallback-level cure.**

- **Responsive locations inspected:** ¶7.1–7.7 (Schedule B allocation and billing of Capital and O&M Costs), ¶12.2 (MIU obtained "in return for their financial investment as identified in Schedule B"), the MIU definition (p0055), ¶13.2/14.1 (upgrade opt-outs), ¶18.1–18.6 (25-year Initial Period, exit only after it, no capital credit on exit), and ¶23 (reclamation without credit).
- **Why it fails fallback:** our Schedule B cost share is fixed for a 25-year Initial Period, with no reduction mechanic and no shortfall true-up; the only "no Party shall be forced" protections cover future upgrades, not the baseline commitment. That is multi-year take-or-pay without a reduction right.
- **Cure chosen:** one inserted subparagraph 7.2A carrying exactly the three fallback elements (12-month limit, 30 days' reduction notice, true-up not penalty). Preferred-level deletion of the cost-sharing model would require rewriting Schedules B and C.
- **Not double-flagged:** the Paragraph 18 exit and Paragraph 23 default mechanics are left untouched for the term/termination rules.
